lessons.idea: The Psalms are the prayer book of Israel and the Church. Mary’s prayer, from the Annunciation to Pentecost, is a model for our prayer: she listens, says yes and prays with the Church.
lessons.question: What do the Psalms and Mary teach about prayer?
lessons.activity: Pray a Psalm in three ways (aloud, sung and silently). Then pray the Magnificat and write your own “magnificat” of thanks.
teach: The Psalms express every human mood and were Jesus’ prayer book (CCC 2585–2589). The Church prays them in the Mass and the Liturgy of the Hours.
Mary’s prayer: the Magnificat (Luke 1:46–55), her presence at Cana, at the Cross and at Pentecost (Acts 1:14) (CCC 2617–2619). She prays for us and with us.
The Hail Mary and the Rosary are Marian prayers that lead to Christ (CCC 2676–2678). The Magnificat is evening prayer each day in the Church.
Praying the Psalms with Jesus helps us pray in dark times too (Psalm 88).
talk: Which Psalm speaks to you now?
What does the Magnificat reveal about Mary?
How does the Rosary help you pray?
quiz: The Psalms are…|The Church’s prayer book|A calendar|A history book|A law code|0|CCC 2585.
The Magnificat is…|A psalm of David|Mary’s song of praise|A hymn of Paul|A creed|1|Luke 1:46.
The Rosary leads us to…|Mary only|Saints only|Christ|Silence|2|CCC 2678.
lessons.life: Pray one psalm each day this week and the Magnificat in the evening.
lessons.saint: Teresa of Calcutta: she began each day with the Magnificat and Mass.
lessons.mem: “My soul magnifies the Lord, and my spirit rejoices in God my Savior.” (Luke 1:46–47)
lessons.hook: Read part of Psalm 22 and Psalm 150. Ask what feelings they show and why the Psalms include both.
lessons.assess: Ask students to pray a psalm and explain what it teaches about prayer.

lessons.title: Guides in prayer: saints and spiritual traditions
lessons.idea: The Church has many schools of prayer taught by saints: Benedictine, Franciscan, Ignatian, Carmelite, Salesian and others. They show that there are many ways to pray and the same Spirit teaches all.
lessons.question: Which school of prayer fits me?
lessons.activity: Sample short practices from three traditions: Benedictine lectio, Ignatian imagination, Carmelite silence. Reflect on which fits, and plan to try one for two weeks.
teach: The saints are guides in prayer (CCC 2683–2684). Each spiritual family has a charism: Benedictine (liturgy and lectio), Franciscan (simplicity, creation), Dominican (study and preaching), Carmelite (contemplation), Ignatian (discernment and finding God in all things), Salesian (devout life for all).
Other guides: the family, pastors, religious communities, catechesis and spiritual direction (CCC 2685–2690). Places and times of prayer support it (CCC 2691–2696).
All schools lead to Christ in the Church (CCC 2684). No method replaces relationship.
Encourage students to ask a trusted guide before taking on intense practices.
talk: Who has taught you to pray?
What practice would you like to try?
Why do we need a guide?
quiz: Ignatian spirituality stresses…|Discernment and finding God in all things|Chant only|Silence only|Work only|0|CCC 2684 context.
A spiritual director is…|A teacher of math|A guide in prayer and life|A judge|A confessor only|1|CCC 2690.
All schools of prayer lead to…|Fame|Christ|A method|Silence|1|CCC 2684.
lessons.life: Try one new practice for two weeks and note what you learn, then talk to a mentor.
lessons.saint: Francis de Sales: he taught that holiness is for everyone and wrote the Introduction to the Devout Life.
misc: “There is only one correct way to pray.”
lessons.mem: “Lord, teach us to pray.” (Luke 11:1)
lessons.hook: Ask students to describe how a favorite athlete or musician practices. Say that saints are coaches in prayer.
lessons.assess: Ask students to describe two schools of prayer and choose a practice.

lessons.title: Obstacles to prayer and persevering
lessons.idea: Prayer is a battle against distraction, dryness, discouragement and acedia. Jesus gave parables of persistence, and the Church teaches humility, trust and perseverance. The Our Father is the school of prayer.
lessons.question: What helps when prayer is hard?
lessons.activity: Make a personal “when prayer is hard” card with five practical steps (return, simplify, sit with a psalm, ask a friend to pray, go to the sacraments). Share one with a partner.
teach: The battle of prayer includes distraction, dryness, presumption and acedia (CCC 2725–2733). A distraction is not a failure; return gently (CCC 2729).
Discouragement and doubt about whether God hears can be answered by humility, trust and persistence (CCC 2734–2741). Jesus says, “Ask, and it will be given you” (Luke 11:9).
Pray without ceasing means making prayer a habit, supported by liturgy and short prayers (CCC 2742–2745). The Our Father is the model.
Seek help if dryness comes with deeper sadness; spiritual direction and counseling both help.
talk: What is your biggest obstacle in prayer?
How do you return after distraction?
Why does Jesus tell us to persist?
quiz: A good response to distraction is…|Gently return to God|Quit|Skip prayer|Get upset|0|CCC 2729.
Acedia is…|Spiritual laziness or discouragement|A feast|A rule|A prayer|0|CCC 2733.
The widow in Luke 18 teaches…|Anger|Persistence|Silence|Fear|1|Luke 18:1.
lessons.life: Choose a fixed time and place to pray for two weeks, and when you wander, return gently.
lessons.saint: Teresa of Calcutta: she experienced long dryness yet kept praying and serving.
misc: “God doesn’t answer unless I feel something.”
lessons.mem: “Pray without ceasing.” (1 Thessalonians 5:17)
lessons.hook: Read the story of the persistent widow (Luke 18:1–8). Ask: “Why does Jesus tell us this?”
lessons.assess: Ask students to name three obstacles and a remedy for each.
